Oracle REST Data Services

Source: vignettes/oracle-ords.Rmd
oracle-ords.Rmd

Oracle REST Data Services (ORDS) exposes selected Oracle tables and database procedures through web APIs. Use it when your Shiny app needs to read Oracle data over HTTPS without installing Oracle client libraries.

oauth_db_oracle_ords_api() reads collections of records and calls custom JSON endpoints with each visitor’s access token. ORDS controls access to those endpoints; the database and endpoint code determine which data they return. For SQL queries through DBI or dbplyr, use the separate Oracle Database guide.

Set up ORDS and sign-in

Ask your administrator for an HTTPS ORDS endpoint exposing the resources your app needs. The example reads an AutoREST collection, which exposes table records as JSON. Use the schema alias URL, including any reverse-proxy prefix, and replace orders with your collection’s name.

ORDS must protect the resource and accept JWT access tokens from your sign-in provider. External-provider JWT profiles require ORDS 23.3 or later; see the ORDS authentication guide for issuer, audience and privilege mappings.

Register your Shiny app with that provider, using http://localhost:8100 as the redirect URI. Request the access scope for the resource and enable refresh tokens if you use offline_access. Save the settings in .Renviron and restart R:

OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-shiny-app-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-shiny-app-client-secret
OAUTHDB_ORDS_ISSUER=https://login.example.org/realms/reporting
OAUTHDB_ORDS_SCOPE=reports.read
OAUTHDB_ORDS_URL=https://data.example.org/ords/reporting

A complete app

After signing in, click Load rows. The app starts its workers once and stops them at shutdown.

pkgs <- c("shiny", "shinyOAuth", "shinyOAuthDB", "mirai", "jsonlite")
for (pkg in pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(pkg)
  }
}

library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

scope <- Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_ORDS_SCOPE")

provider <- oauth_provider_oidc_discover(
  issuer = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_ORDS_ISSUER")
)

client <- oauth_client(
  provider,
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100",
  scopes = c("openid", "profile", "offline_access", scope),
  required_scopes = scope
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
    actionButton("load", "Load rows"),
    verbatimTextOutput("rows")
  ),
  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

fetch_rows <- function(database) {
  database$select("orders", query = list(limit = 20L))$items
}

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server(
    "auth",
    client,
    auto_redirect = FALSE,
    async = TRUE
  )
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())
  ords <- oauth_db_oracle_ords_api(
    auth$connection,
    url = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_ORDS_URL"),
    required_scopes = scope
  )
  query_task <- oauth_db_task(ords, method = fetch_rows)
  observeEvent(input$load, {
    query_task$invoke()
  })
  output$rows <- renderPrint(query_task$result())
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, uiPattern = ".*", onStart = function() {
    mirai::daemons(2)
    onStop(function() mirai::daemons(0))
  }),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

# Open the app in your regular browser at its registered redirect URI.

Save this as example.R, run source("example.R"), and open http://localhost:8100 in a regular browser. Sign in to read one page of the collection. Results are JSON lists, with records in items. Use offset and limit to fetch further pages; the client doesn’t follow pagination links automatically.

For a custom JSON handler, call its relative path:

result <- ords$request(
  c("api", "sales"),
  query = list(country = "NL"),
  trailing_slash = TRUE
)

select() handles AutoREST collection paths. For a custom endpoint, request() uses the path you supply; set trailing_slash = TRUE if it needs one. See ?oauth_db_oracle_ords_api for other request methods and raw responses.

User identity and data access

ORDS validates the JWT and enforces its resource privileges. The JWT subject is available to handlers as :current_user. An ORDS role is not automatically an Oracle database role, and accepting a user JWT does not by itself change the database schema used by a handler. Configure handler filtering or a supported end-user security context to enforce the required per-user data access. Verify two users with different permissions before deployment.

Each call uses a current token and discards results after sign-out or account changes. Read requests can refresh and retry once after HTTP 401; writes don’t retry automatically. The client returns your custom handler’s JSON without interpreting application-specific status fields.
